cultural_context.description: Delhi is a cosmopolitan capital with layered historical, religious, artistic, culinary, and urban traditions. Its cultural identity reflects centuries of interaction among different communities and the coexistence of historic areas such as Shahjahanabad with a modern metropolitan city.
cultural_context.important_note: Delhi is a Union Territory and the National Capital Territory rather than a state. Cultural practices vary across neighborhoods, communities, religions, families, generations, and individual contexts. Information in this file should not be treated as universal to every person in Delhi.

source.organization: Delhi Tourism, Government of NCT of Delhi
source.title: Delhi Tourism

communication_guidance: Delhi is highly diverse, so do not assume that one language, accent, religion, or communication style represents the whole city.
Use respectful communication with local residents, shopkeepers, workers, hosts, and people in religious or heritage spaces.
In Old Delhi and other culturally significant areas, follow local venue and community guidance when participating in religious or cultural activities.
greetings_and_communication.limitation: The current verified knowledge base does not contain a sufficiently sourced everyday Delhi phrase list. Do not invent local phrases or translations.

verified_information.description: Delhi Tourism describes the city as having diverse cuisine and food experiences. Official tourism material highlights Old Delhi and other areas for food and culinary exploration.

source.title: Delhi Tourism

verified_information.description: Official tourism material describes Chandni Chowk and Old Delhi as important food areas and documents traditional Mughlai food experiences in the area.

dining_guidance: Delhi's food culture is highly diverse; do not assume that Old Delhi cuisine represents every neighborhood or community.
Food preferences and dietary practices vary by religion, community, family, and individual choice.
Respect individual dietary choices and follow local hosts' guidance at traditional meals or community events.
food_and_dining.limitation: The verified knowledge base does not establish universal everyday dining etiquette for every community in Delhi.

source.title: Delhi

traditional_clothing.description: Traditional clothing seen in Delhi can include garments such as sarees, salwar-kameez, kurta-pajama, sherwanis, and other regional or community-specific attire. Clothing varies by community, religion, occasion, and personal preference.

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Multi-faith heritage
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Delhi includes significant Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Jain, Bahá'í, and other religious sites. Visitors should follow the specific rules and customs of each place.

source.organization: Delhi Tourism, Government of NCT of Delhi
source.title: Faith and Heritage

visitor_guidance: Treat temples, mosques, gurdwaras, shrines, and other religious spaces with respect.
Follow each venue's rules regarding footwear, clothing, photography, prayer times, and access.
At Jama Masjid and similar religious sites, be especially attentive to prayer timings and clothing requirements; follow current instructions displayed by the venue.
Ask before photographing people, religious ceremonies, performers, or culturally significant activities when permission is unclear.
Do not assume Old Delhi or Mughal-era traditions represent all of Delhi.
Do not assume the practices of one religious or cultural community apply to the whole city.
During major festivals and heritage events, follow crowd-management, safety, and venue instructions.
Respect Delhi's residential neighborhoods and local communities rather than treating cultural areas only as tourist attractions.
